# CPDataKit v0.10.0

CSV imports in the local workbench now preview the actual columns and require explicit field,
type, unit and role declarations before saving confirmed data. Select the delimiter, header/unit
rows, decimal separator and UTF-8/BOM or GB18030 encoding without editing JSON. Original bytes,
the source digest, excluded columns, schema and import receipt remain available for inspection.
Invalid rows, missing numeric units and unsafe numeric conversions stop the import.

Verified conversion snapshots can be selected as project inputs with their original schema.
Repeated selections reuse the catalog record. Changed, missing, linked or cross-project snapshots
are rejected. Newly written HDF5 files preserve column creation order; explicit selections keep
caller order. Historical files without order metadata retain their existing ordering.

Selection changes clear stale mapping and schema drafts, and asynchronous responses cannot
replace another selection's authoring state. CSV errors include the API's suggested correction.
Frontend verification runs isolated VM scenarios in one Node process, observes background
completion and retains its 15-second limit. Hosted CI records Node and platform identities.

Try the synthetic three-row [CSV example](../../examples/csv-intake/README.md).
The real-case acceptance script verifies the identity of the separately obtained CC BY 4.0
Mendeley IN718 archive (DOI 10.17632/nx55jj48rx.2), all 12 CSV files and 24,073 rows before
producing a success receipt. The archive and local research data are not included in the package.

This minor version adds public workflows while retaining the existing HDF5 1.0 contract and
Python >=3.12 requirement. No runtime dependency, license or publishing-permission change is
introduced. The historical NetCDF3 datetime limitation remains documented in
[the known issue](../../docs/known-issues/netcdf3-datetime.md).

Validation and release evidence: [2026-10-01 review](../../docs/verification/2026-10-01-release-review.md).
